I did not do this because the `lg2::` does not take much space and prevents name collision.

So if we want to define any function like `info` or `warning` then it is no longer possible because there is already such a function in scope from lg2.

Even in the definition of `PHOSPHOR_LOG2_USING` itself they describe this problem of name collision.

```
 81 /** Handy scope-level `using` to get the necessary bits of lg2. */
 82 #define PHOSPHOR_LOG2_USING                                                    \
 83     using lg2::emergency;                                                      \
 84     using lg2::alert;                                                          \
 85     using lg2::critical;                                                       \
 86     using lg2::error;                                                          \
 87     using lg2::warning;                                                        \
 88     using lg2::notice;                                                         \
 89     using lg2::info;                                                           \
 90     using lg2::debug
 91 // We purposefully left out `using lg2::log` above to avoid collisions with
 92 // the math function `log`.  There is little use for direct calls to `lg2::log`,
 93 // when the level-aliases are available, since it is just a more awkward syntax.
```

There is another issue which is greppability. In `dbus-sensors` grepping for `debug` would also shows us `static bool debug` in which case `lg2::debug` is more grep friendly.

@spinler@us.ibm.com @ed@tanous.net what do you think, do we have to have this `PHOSPHOR_LOG2_USING` ?


@christopher.meis@9elements.com is this a blocking comment for you or do you consider the `PHOSPHOR_LOG2_USING` to be an optional improvement to this patch?

I looked into https://isocpp.github.io/CppCoreGuidelines/CppCoreGuidelines#sf6-use-using-namespace-directives-for-transition-for-foundation-libraries-such-as-std-or-within-a-local-scope-only

and they recommend `using` the namespace if it would be verbose and distracting otherwise. Now `lg2` qualifies as a foundational library for OpenBMC but 'verbose' and 'distracting' is more subjective.
Not a huge deal for me, but I agree with you.  if it was a long namespace name then it's one thing, but 'lg2' is about as short as one can get.
I haven't tried it, but I can't imagine the \n works.
Thanks for the quick review. Fixed it 👍.
